subtopic: The Modulus and the Conjugate of a Complex Number
title: Modulus & conjugate: the toolkit

board_content.latex: \overline{z_1 z_2}=\bar z_1\bar z_2;\ \ \overline{\left(\tfrac{z_1}{z_2}\right)}=\tfrac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2};\ \ \overline{z^{\,n}}=(\bar z)^{n}

board_content.text: On the unit circle, where $|z|=1$, the conjugate equals the reciprocal: $\bar z=\tfrac{1}{z}$.
The one identity to internalize: $z\bar z=|z|^2$.

segments_english.text: Here is the whole toolkit on one board — your consolidated reference for modulus and conjugate.
The conjugate is a minus i b. Adding z and its conjugate gives twice the real part; subtracting gives two i times the imaginary part.
The workhorse: z times z bar equals the modulus squared, which is a squared plus b squared.
Conjugation over operations: the conjugate of a product is the product of conjugates, of a quotient the quotient of conjugates, and of a power the power of the conjugate.
Modulus over operations: the modulus of a product is the product of moduli, of a quotient the quotient of moduli, and of a power the power of the modulus.
The inverse, cleanly: z inverse equals z bar over the modulus squared, which is a minus i b over a squared plus b squared.
And a favourite special case: when z sits on the unit circle, so its modulus is one, the conjugate equals the reciprocal, one over z. That substitution simplifies a huge number of problems.
If you internalize only one line from this board, make it this: z times z bar equals modulus squared. Everything downstream leans on it.

segments_hinglish.text: Ye raha poora toolkit ek board par — modulus aur conjugate ke liye aapka consolidated reference.
Conjugate hai a minus i b. z aur uske conjugate ko add karne se milta hai twice real part; subtract karne se two i times imaginary part.
Workhorse: z times z bar barabar modulus squared, jo hai a square plus b square.
Conjugation operations par: product ka conjugate hai conjugates ka product, quotient ka quotient, aur power ka conjugate ki wahi power.
Modulus operations par: product ka modulus hai moduli ka product, quotient ka quotient, aur power ka modulus ki wahi power.
Inverse, cleanly: z inverse barabar z bar over modulus squared, jo hai a minus i b over a square plus b square.
Aur ek favourite special case: jab z unit circle par ho, to modulus one, conjugate barabar reciprocal, one over z. Ye substitution bahut saare problems simplify karti hai.
Agar is board se sirf ek line internalize karni ho, to ye karo: z times z bar barabar modulus squared. Aage sab kuch isi par tika hai.
